name: Mushroom Gravy Pork Chops

fit.note: 582 cal is within 400-650; 18g carb is under the 35g cap; pork, no seafood; sear-and-simmer skillet scales cleanly to 14 servings.

dedup.catalog: KEEP - closest catalog dish is creamy-mushroom-pork-chops-over-mashed-potatoes (pork chops + mushroom sauce + skillet), but that one is a white heavy-cream sauce served OVER MASHED POTATOES; this is a starchless low-carb BROWN mushroom gravy (chicken broth + beef bouillon + Worcestershire + Kitchen Bouquet browning, only 1/3 cup half-and-half). Brown-gravy vs cream-sauce plus no-starch vs mashed-potato genuinely distinguish the plate for a low-carb run.
dedup.pool: Distinct from already-accepted creamy-garlic-herb-wine-pork-chops (line 13 of accepted-slugs): that shares wine+cream+garlic+herb+skillet+pork, but it is a clear garlic-herb white-wine CREAM sauce with NO mushrooms; this candidate's identity is 8 oz mushrooms in a brown gravy. Different plate.

borderline.reason: 3-of-4 structural overlap (protein=pork chop, method=skillet sear+simmer, mushroom sauce family) with catalog creamy-mushroom-pork-chops-over-mashed-potatoes. Kept as distinct on brown-gravy-vs-cream and starchless-vs-mashed-potato, but flagging for audit to confirm it reads as a separate catalog entry rather than a near-dup.

cross_protein_collision: A brown mushroom-gravy sear-and-simmer skillet is a protein-swappable frame: the same dish exists with beef, turkey, or chicken. Watch for a same-sauce twin - notably salisbury-steak-mushroom-gravy-skillet is in this run's pool (beef + mushroom brown gravy; distinct only by ground-patty format), and any 'turkey/chicken mushroom gravy skillet' would be structurally identical. Decider should cross-check the beef/turkey lanes.
